summary: Light on Spectacle Island at Port Mouton: lit 1873, a government lifeboat station near it from 1889, owned by a local society since late 2015.

structures.note: Register gives 7.5 m (25 ft); LighthouseFriends and NSLPS give 28 ft.

staffing.note: Final keeper Harvey L. Huskins, 1954-1961, is the last name on LighthouseFriends' keeper list. Automated by 1993 (NSLPS).

access.note: Reached by boat (NSLPS). Visible from Route 3 between Summerville Beach and Hunts Point (Region of Queens).

events.note: Light put in operation 1 September 1873
Square wooden tower built by G. S. Parker for $665
Lightning struck the tower on 16 June 1882, shattering the lantern room and splitting the south wall
Port Mouton lifeboat station established by the Department of Marine (coxswain and crew of seven)
Heavy seas carried away the wharf at the landing; a new wharf was built
Keeper Edward McPherson drowned 5 May 1892
Hand-operated foghorn given to the keeper
Fourth-order Fresnel lens installed (LighthouseFriends)
Light changed from fixed red to fixed white (LighthouseFriends; NSLPS dates the fixed white and 4th-order dioptric lens to 1922)
Keeper's dwelling destroyed by fire; new dwelling built in 1922
New square wooden tower replaced the 1873 tower
Present tower built 1937 (register)
LighthouseFriends' keeper list ends with Huskins in 1961
Automated by 1993 (NSLPS)
Coast Guard reported to be considering demolition; local residents rallied to save the tower
Tower extensively repaired
Lead-contaminated soil around the lighthouse removed by helicopter, 9 December 2011
Declared a heritage lighthouse 2 February 2015
Spectacle Light Society gained ownership in late 2015, with a $43,000 federal grant
Floating dock installed at the island to improve access
NSLPS list: hand fog horn in answer to vessels (1930). LighthouseFriends dates a hand-operated foghorn to 1906.

corrections.why: The society's name on the NSLPS list and its Facebook page, and in LighthouseFriends, is Spectacle Light Society.

The record's point is from OpenStreetMap. The Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights (H3742) gives the light at 43 55 05.6 N, 064 48 14.4 W; the NSLPS coordinates agree with it. The record's point is about 90 m away. Reviewer to confirm.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends dates the fourth-order lens and fixed white light to 1915. The NSLPS list dates a fourth-order dioptric lens, fixed white, to 1922. The story gives both dates and does not choose between them.
LighthouseFriends' visitor note says the Coast Guard owns the lighthouse, but its own history says the society gained ownership in late 2015. The story follows the 2015 account.
LighthouseFriends' history names Anna McPherson; its keeper list gives Mrs. E. McPherson for the same years. Both appear in the story.

The Coast Guard list and NSLPS place the light on the northeast point of Spectacle Island; the Region of Queens says the northwestern point. The story gives the northeast point and states the municipality's version.
LighthouseFriends dates a hand-operated foghorn given to the keeper to 1906; NSLPS dates a hand fog horn to 1930. The story gives both and does not choose.

The Region of Queens gives the wreck dates (Clifford J. White 1916, Ethel Emerson 1884); no primary record was found in the corpus. The story attributes them to the municipality and says they are unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: Main source is LighthouseFriends, which quotes the 1873 and 1877 Department of Marine reports and an interview with Chris Mills (The Lightkeeper) about Huskins. Pre-1900 Canadian reports are not in the corpus, so those facts are second-hand; the Huskins anecdote is quoted as one short sentence only (copyright). Register text read from HistoricPlaces.ca 20719; the record's 7.5 m tower height is the register's search snippet figure and the cached page does not show it, so it is not cited; LighthouseFriends and NSLPS give 28 ft. Keeper gap 1937 to 1954: none named in any source read. The Marine keeper and wharfinger tables in the corpus (1905 to 1910) list 'Port Mouton' lines, including a Geo. Cook who is a wharfinger, not a keeper; none was matched to this light by column position, so none is cited. The Region of Queens wreck names (Clifford J. White 1916, Ethel Emerson 1884, Dart 1852) were searched in the corpus with no hit, and remain unconfirmed. Life-saving station (1889) is a separate station record and may need its own page. Register number on the record (20719) matches the page read. Parks Canada's DFHD page was not readable. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the story now gives the Region of Queens' northwestern-point placement against the northeast point in the Coast Guard list and NSLPS; the 1906 hand-operated foghorn (LighthouseFriends) against the 1930 hand fog horn (NSLPS); the 1915 (LighthouseFriends) and 1922 (NSLPS) lens dates as disagreeing; the Region of Queens wreck dates as the municipality's own, unconfirmed; and it no longer says resident keeping ended in 1961, since LighthouseFriends' list simply ends with Huskins. The 1911 Marine keeper table (scan p. 259, printed p. 257) was checked against the page image on 2026-10-27: the Port Mouton row reads J. Oscar Campbell, appointed April 29, 1898, which agrees with LighthouseFriends; not cited in the story. The 1873 and 1877 Department reports are quoted through LighthouseFriends, the only source read for them (pre-1900 Canadian reports are not in the corpus). About a dozen LighthouseFriends passages were reworded under the copyright rule.
